minutes.headline: Planning Board continued both the water protection and battery storage bylaw hearings, and took no position on a Howard Street land purchase.
minutes.summary: The board approved a master plan committee member, closed out the Homan Street rain garden agreements, and heard long public comment on the water supply protection bylaw (Zone 1 removal concerns at Hickory Hills). Both bylaw hearings were continued to April 8; the board also voted to give no recommendation on the right of first refusal for 100 Howard Street.

public_comment.topic: Asked to lead the pledge; board asked that it be done before the meeting opens.
Opposed removing Zone 1 protections at Hickory Hills given the water district easement; asked the board to withdraw the article, do a site visit.
Asked that the 1987 Zone 1 protections for boating, fishing, and conservation be kept.
Asked what protections are lost if town Zone 1 rules are removed.
Supported Zone 2 and 3 changes for clients; no objection to keeping Zone 1 language.

public_comment.speaker_as_heard: Mike (open space chair), 41 Stone Fence Road
public_comment.topic: Urged use of day-night sound level (LDN) in the battery storage bylaw noise standard.
Said the parcel price figure was understated; later said the land is of little public value.
Boards should base recommendations on their own goals rather than finances.
Disappointed when boards give no recommendation; voters rely on them.

Continue the public hearing for 255 Sunny Hill Road to April 22nd at 6:05.
Continue the water supply protection and battery energy storage bylaw public hearing to April 8th at 6:05 p.m.
Issue certificates of completion for 147 and 159 Homan.
Release the performance guarantee for 147 and 159 Homan.

budget_items.topic: Performance guarantee / tri-party agreement funds, Homan Street rain gardens
budget_items.what_was_said: Developer sought return of funds held under the tri-party agreement; board voted to release the guarantee.

budget_items.topic: Cost of exercising right of first refusal on 100 Howard Street
budget_items.what_was_said: Members discussed the parcel price and the lack of appetite to spend on it amid a possible override.
Surety capped relative to estimated cost with inflation adjustment, mirroring the solar bylaw.

decisions.decision: Board agreed to consider revising the water bylaw to reinsert Zone 1 protections, dropping special permit requirements, pending easement documents from residents.
Agreed to add a Chapter 61 checkbox to relevant applications and to invite the open space committee to a future meeting.
Board was fine with the staff reformatting of application forms with no vote needed.
Small battery storage definition to be revised to allow 1-4 residential units without requiring an EV charger.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board continued the water supply protection and battery energy storage bylaw hearings to April 8th, with no vote on either bylaw's text.
The board agreed to consider restoring Zone 1 protections in the water bylaw and dropping special permit requirements, pending easement documents from residents.
The board voted to send the Select Board a message that it has no recommendation on the right of first refusal for 100 Howard Street.
The board voted to issue certificates of completion and release the performance guarantee for 147 and 159 Homan Street.
The board approved a member-at-large application to the master plan steering committee and continued the 255 Sunny Hill Road hearing to April 22nd.

why_it_matters: The water bylaw decides what can be built or done in protected zones around the town's water supply, and residents near Hickory Hills spoke against losing Zone 1 protections before any final text exists.

The Planning Board gave the Select Board no recommendation on 100 Howard Street, so any decision on exercising the town's right of first refusal, a possible spending question, rests without that board's advice.
The battery storage bylaw sets noise, surety and definition rules for future installations, and its wording is still being revised.
